name: intercom
label: Intercom
note: Intercom's REST API with an access token. This entry is the api.intercom.io host only; a workspace hosted on another regional host needs an upstream naming it.

name: intercom-eu
label: Intercom (EU)
note: Intercom for a workspace whose data Intercom hosts in the European Union. The token and its placement are identical to the intercom entry and only the host differs, so a workspace hosted in the United States belongs on that one instead.

name: front
label: Front
note: Front's Core API with an API token made under Settings, Developers. The token carries only the features, namespaces and permissions chosen when it was created, so a call outside them is refused by Front rather than by us.

name: pylon
label: Pylon
note: Pylon's API with an API token. This is the United States region; Pylon runs a separate European one at api.eu.usepylon.com, and a token belongs to whichever of the two holds the workspace.

name: pylon-eu
label: Pylon (EU)
note: Pylon's European region, named as a server in Pylon's own API definition beside the United States one. Same token placement as the pylon entry; only the host differs.

name: plain
label: Plain
note: Plain's API with a machine user's API key. The whole API is one GraphQL endpoint that accepts POST alone, so every operation arrives at the same path and what a request actually does is inside its body, not in its URL.

name: unthread
label: Unthread
note: Unthread's API with a service account key sent as X-Api-Key. Unthread's own reference contradicts itself about the value — the authentication section says the key alone, one upload example writes "Bearer " in front of it — and this entry sends the key alone, which is what the authentication section says.

name: missive
label: Missive
note: Missive's REST API with an API token from your Missive preferences. Missive issues no organisation-level or shared-account token, so the key is one person's and reaches every account that person can reach, including shared ones.

name: trengo
label: Trengo
note: Trengo's REST API with the access token found under Settings, Integrations, Rest API.

name: kustomer
label: Kustomer
note: Kustomer's API with a key from Settings, Security, API Keys. The key's roles are fixed when it is issued, so what it may read is Kustomer's decision and not one this service can narrow.

name: devrev
label: DevRev
note: DevRev's public API with a personal access token. DevRev names every endpoint as a flat verb rather than a resource tree, so the read that proves a token is dev-users.self.

name: groove
label: Groove
note: Groove's API with an access token. Groove also accepts the same token as an access_token query parameter; this entry sends it in the Authorization header instead, which keeps a live credential out of URLs and out of whatever logs them.

name: freshdesk
template_hint: the name in your Freshdesk address — acme in acme.freshdesk.com
label: Freshdesk
note: Freshdesk with an agent's API key, which Freshdesk reads as the basic-auth username and whose password it ignores — that is what the empty password here means. A helpdesk answering on its own vanity domain rather than a name under freshdesk.com needs an upstream giving that address in full.

name: freshservice
template_hint: the name in your Freshservice address — acme in acme.freshservice.com
label: Freshservice
note: Freshservice with a personal API key as the basic-auth username; Freshservice's own documentation says any dummy password will do, so this entry sends none. Username-and-password basic authentication was withdrawn in 2023 and only the key works.
